requirement:
Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name, or with a built-in name under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, and MAY use the `{fixme}` role in fenced form. A reference MAY instead be written in fenced form, `:::{role} name` on one line, a body, and a closing fence, following the fence rules of {cite}`requirements.ci.span` and {cite}`requirements.ci.fence_lengths`; the fenced form is the same edge with attached commentary, and the inline form carries none. In a source comment, fence lines MUST be recognized after removing each line's comment delimiters within one comment run under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, and a fence that does not close within its comment run MUST be a validation error. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. The roles MUST mean:

- `{cite}`: the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition. It is an
  edge from the source to the definition.
- `{impl}`: the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision,
  performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition
  specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining
  one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or
  producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as
  implementing it. A check MUST count only if the definition states it, or the
  source could not meet one of the definition's obligations without it; source
  that checks it is consistent with a definition, such as recognizing a form the
  definition specifies in order to decide whether to run other behavior, relies
  on that definition and calls for `{cite}`. A requirement stating a convention
  for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by
  the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that
  collects and reports those outputs.
- `{test}`: the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies:
  a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome,
  or a named example through the concrete case it describes.
- `{fixme}`: the source acknowledges a known gap in fulfilling the definition. It
  MUST use the fenced form, and its body MUST describe the gap. The body MAY
  begin with option lines naming issues that track the gap, one per line, in the
  form `:github: <owner>/<repo>#<number>`, such as
  `:github: rust-lang/rust#123`. `github` MUST be the only recognized option.
  A named `{fixme}` MAY appear only in sources outside the book. Validation MUST report
  any other option line, a `:github:` value not in that form, an inline
  `{fixme}`, a `{fixme}` in a requirement or example declaration, and a
  `{fixme}` whose body, without option lines and comment delimiters, is empty.
  An unnamed `{fixme}`, a fence of `:::{fixme}` with no name, MAY appear in any
  project text, including a requirement or example body, to tie that place to
  the issues it names. It MUST have at least one `:github:` option line and MAY
  have a description; it is not a reference edge, acknowledges no gap, needs no
  coverage, and does not count as a reference for Rust item coverage. Its
  issues are checked under {cite}`requirements.cli.fixme_issues`.

`{impl}`, `{test}`, and `{fixme}` are edges from the definition to the source.
Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the
definitions it implements or tests.

```text
{impl}`requirements.references.roles`
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`
{test}`requirements.references.roles`
```
rationale:
I found no gap in the code or tests for `requirements.references.roles`.

**Comment fences and unclosed fences**
- Comment-run fences:
  - Obligation: in a source comment, fence lines are recognized after removing each line's comment delimiters within one comment run.
  - Code: `src/fenced.rs#fn[comment_fences]` builds lines per comment run using `strip_comment_delimiters`, and `src/fenced.rs#fn[source_fences]` dispatches to it.
  - Tests: `comment_delimiters_are_removed_per_line` and `comment_fences_close_within_one_comment_run`. The latter also checks that a later run's fence does not close an earlier one.
- Unclosed fence:
  - Obligation: a fence that does not close within its comment run is a validation error.
  - Code: `src/evidence.rs#fn[validate_references]`, in its `unclosed` branch.
  - Test: `fenced_references_in_comments_and_built_in_rules_are_validated` asserts the "has no closing fence" error for the unclosed fence.

**`{fixme}` rules**
All of these are implemented in `src/evidence.rs#fn[validate_fixme_form]`, with option parsing in `src/fixme.rs` (`FixmeBody`).
- An inline `{fixme}` is reported.
- A named `{fixme}` in a declaration, or in the book outside a declaration, is reported.
- An option line other than `:github:` is reported, as is a `:github:` value not in `<owner>/<repo>#<number>` form (via `FixmeBody` problems).
- A named `{fixme}` with an empty body is reported.
- An unnamed `{fixme}` with no `:github:` line is reported.

The test `fixme_references_are_fenced_described_and_named_only_outside_the_book` asserts every one of these errors. `fixme_bodies_split_github_options_from_their_description` unit-tests the option and body parsing.

**Unnamed `{fixme}` is not an edge**
- No edge and no gap acknowledgment:
  - Code: `validate_fixme_form` returns false for an unnamed `{fixme}`. `validate_references` then skips it because its name is empty, so it never enters `by_definition` or the fixme entries that acknowledge gaps.
  - Test: the same test asserts that an unnamed `{fixme}` in the book and in source produces no coverage error.
- Not counted for Rust item coverage: `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[unreferenced_items]` excludes `Fixme` in its `counts` closure. `a_fixme_does_not_count_as_an_items_reference` tests this.

**Edge directions and role meanings**
- `{cite}` is not part of a definition's evidence, while `{impl}`, `{test}` and `{fixme}` are. This is implemented in `validate_references` (the `Cite` filter) and tested by `uncovered_cite_is_not_reported_while_uncovered_impl_and_test_are`.
- Which edges feed a subject's mandatory inputs is tested by `only_edges_leaving_the_subject_contribute_inputs`.
- The impl, test and cite semantics are guidance for reviewing sources. They need no separate code, because the reference model does not change them.

Other `{impl}`-marked items:
- `src/evidence.rs#fn[declaration_line_ranges]` supports the declaration-placement check.
- `validate_references` covers the edge-resolution and built-in handling.

```text

{cite}`requirements.references.roles`
{test}`requirements.references.roles`
:::{req} builtin_definitions
Habeas MUST provide built-in definitions named `habeas:<name>`, available in
every project without a declaration. Each built-in MUST have fixed text, which
states its obligations and is documented in Habeas's reference documentation, and
MUST state which reference roles may use it. References MUST resolve built-in
names alongside project definitions. So that every book stands alone, the book
MUST render a reference to a built-in as a badge without a link whose hover text
gives the built-in's full text. Built-ins MUST NOT require or permit evidence
files and MUST NOT appear in the requirements index, `habeas status`, or the
missing-evidence check of {cite}`requirements.ci.coverage`. A project definition
MUST NOT use a full name beginning with `habeas:`; validation MUST report one,
and the `:` character already makes such names invalid under
{cite}`requirements.ci.identifiers`. Validation MUST report a reference to a
built-in in a role the built-in does not permit, or that breaks the built-in's
stated form.
:::{req} span

A `{req}` definition MUST use an opening fence of at least three colons immediately followed by `{req} <name>`. A closing fence MUST have at least as many colons as the opening fence and nothing else on its line except whitespace. As in CommonMark fences, an opening or closing fence MAY be indented by up to three spaces; a line indented by four or more spaces MUST NOT be a fence. The requirement body MUST be all Markdown between those fence lines, including headings, examples, diagrams, and blank lines, and MUST NOT include text after the closing fence. Leading and trailing whitespace MUST be excluded when comparing the body with evidence.
:::{req} fence_lengths

A `{req}` opening fence MAY contain four or more colons. Habeas MUST accept opening fences of any length of at least three colons. A colon-only line with fewer colons than the opener MUST remain inside the requirement body, allowing a nested colon directive. A closing fence outside a fenced code example with at least as many colons as the opener MUST end the body.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
:::{req} fixme_issues
`habeas status` MUST look up, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.github_reads`,
every issue that a `:github:` option line of a named or unnamed `{fixme}` under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles` names, and MUST report each `{fixme}`
naming an issue that is closed or does not exist as an error, with its file and
line and the issue. It MUST also report the item that contains that `{fixme}` as
failing: the outline node containing it, or the requirement or example
declaration whose body contains it, in the same way it reports an uncovered
Rust item. When GitHub cannot be reached, the issue MUST be assumed open.
Repository validation MUST NOT contact GitHub.
